headword: {最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ}
reading: さいこうさいばんしょ

definitions.gloss: Supreme Court; highest court of law
definitions.explanation: The highest judicial authority in a country. In Japan, the Supreme Court (located in Tokyo) serves as the court of last resort and has the power of judicial review over the constitutionality of laws.

examples.japanese: {最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{判決|はんけつ}→判決：05906_hanketsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}した→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: The Supreme Court issued a ruling.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{事件|じけん}→事件：01568_jiken⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ}⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{争|あらそ}われた→争う：01866_arasou⟧。
examples.english: This case was fought all the way to the Supreme Court.

examples.japanese: {最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{裁判官|さいばんかん}→裁判官：09562_saibankan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{国民審査|こくみんしんさ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{審査|しんさ}→審査：08375_shinsa⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Supreme Court justices are reviewed through a national referendum.

notes: Compound of ⟦{最高|さいこう}→最高：02637_saikou⟧ (highest/supreme) + ⟦{裁判所|さいばんしょ}→裁判所：09665_saibansho⟧ (court of law). Commonly abbreviated to {最高裁|さいこうさい} in news and conversation. Japan's court system has three levels: {簡易裁判所|かんいさいばんしょ} / {地方裁判所|ちほうさいばんしょ} (district courts), {高等裁判所|こうとうさいばんしょ} (high courts), and {最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ} (Supreme Court). The Chief Justice ({長官|ちょうかん}) is appointed by the Emperor on the advice of the Cabinet.
